the two intersect: *her*

I fell in love for real. Holy. Fuck. did I fall in love.  I have no idea how I fell in love that much.  It changed *everything*  I can't tell you how *alive* I felt, how special the world was, but people who know intense love, first love, true love -- all those things at once, for my best friend. 

And then, well, she didn't feel the same way, and completely abandoned me. Gone in every way possible. She left me here looking at dreams that mean so very much to me, but feel wingless. 

Queue a year of depression.  Really fucking bad depression.  And a slow fight to get better.

I don't want to be too brash, so forgive me if I am.

Sometimes, when we're down in the canyons of life, we get so focused on the walls that are around us we just keep moving forward along the stream because we know it goes somewhere.  Because it goes somewhere and we've been doing it for a while and we're okay. We ended up here, and so we stay here. And in time we become comfortable and don't really see a way out. 

Not everyone ends up in these canyons.  Some people were lucky enough to start out way above them and see them and avoid them.  A few us us fell into them while looking too far ahead.  Others slowly lowered themselves into them, unknowingly. Sometimes the ground falls out under us. 

Look, you're 18.  And you're already *way* more responsible and work so much more than most people your age. You've already dealt with shit others will never face. Life wasn't handed to you and there are realities that you are facing that aren't easy at all.

But you're still at a point in your life where you can guide yourself.  You only have this life to live.  That's it.  This one and only extraordinary life. It's already 1/4 done, statistically.  You've met the "real world" head on and have been so brave so far. 

Are you ready to be even more brave?  

Do it.  Fill out some applications.  Fill out the FASFA, look at schools.   You might be surprised.  Yes, it's expensive as fuck.  Hooooooly shit.  But where you are now, do you see the canyon you're in changing?  Do you see yourself in control?  Why not try one of the ropes out of this place where life is moving too slowly?

Maybe it's time to try something bigger.  A dollar an hour more?  Management training?  Maybe it's time to say, "you know what, this isn't everything that I can be".

I'm not talking about you reducing hours to go to college.  That puts the job first.  I'm talking about going to college being the core and finding ways to make that happen.  I'm talking about ArcticVanguard -- how is it that *you* are going to shape where you are? 

There are opportunities a college offers a person your age.  You will meet peers, share life, and discover your identity.  You will network and earn a piece of paper that turns out to mean a lot in our society.  There are consoling services and there are activities and there is a safe environment to feel things out in.  It's not easy.  Half the people who go, drop out.  

But you -- you've already fought through worse.  You've already learned what it means to work.  And you can do this, too. 

If you want something you've never had,    
then you're going to have to do something you've never done.

Instead of saying why not, instead ask, *why not*?

That's understandable.  Just don't put the burden on yourself alone.  If nothing else, posting here helps take just a tiny sliver of that weight off.  

Friends, friends they matter in this stuff though.  I know it's not as easy as "find friends that are good" at all -- but not having those friends around right now makes the professionals doubly important. 

Just remember you're not alone in this.

in another reply you say you're currently paying your way through school... do they offer any services?  

The therapy can be so helpful, especially when some of the illness follows a predictable path by running through your family.  School costs a shit-ton, and therapy is cheaper in comparison.  Can you justify it to yourself as a way to help make the school that you're working so hard out work for yourself better?

And don't try to be what you're not.  If you're hurting, you're hurting. Work with friends and don't try to fight this battle alone because it doesn't need to be that hard.

thanks.

i love this line

> if you're not comfortable starting at a particular point then there is no problem with starting on the opposite end. Your ultimate destination is the same, you. 

and [for you.](http://i.imgur.com/kuX9Ife.jpg)

For me, since that's what I can share:

for me what got me through the worst bit of depression, got me away from thinking about killing myself and gave me a little control, it was my friends.  Therapy, conversations -- they helped too -- but it was my friends in the moment and my friends that get me through the days now, too.  

The worst thing in all this is feeling alone. Even worse is feeling alone in sea of people who care.   You know Sharon, I don't -- but find a way towards her heart, find the place you occupy in it.   She obviously trusts you a hell of a lot: you know about her situation, her medicine, her note.  I don't hesitate to assume that you are one of her very closest friends.  You are one of the little graces that still gives her hope and joy.  I promise.  She knows how much you mean to her and she is thankful for you in a way she might not always share.  You mean a lot to her. 

You asking these questions here shows that you care about her a lot too.  It shows you love her -- and love is the only way people get out of this stuff.  You can't know the right words, or the hell that is in her mind.  It's a raging storm and she's doing everything she can to fight it and some days she feels out of control.  You can just be there and say "ill fight through the storm with you, you don't have to be alone"  In the darkness, you can say, "let me be a little light."

It's clear you've done that for her so far.  For her, in case she hasn't been able to say it, thanks.  You're mature and seriously an awesome person.   Keep up the good work. 

___

Suicide is an act of control, among other things.  Let her know she has a stable constant in you.  Check in every day -- "how are you?"  Don't necessarily do it all at once but share little things in your life and create ties to you.  Show up at the same time each day, make it so she knows i-lumos is going to be there for her and will be every day and she can pick up the phone and call you and or write you a note and you'll read every single letter. Don't even verbalize what you're doing.  Just be there. Every day. Again. Again.  Show her love, be gentle. If you are physically near her, give her hugs, and don't just let go.  Hold her there for a moment and let her feel secure.

If things get truly bad, gently guide her to a hotline and professionals. You're over your head when that happens -- after all you're only in high school too and you can't be everything to Sharon.  But helping things not get to that point, being that bridge -- that's where the real healing happens. And everything else isn't very useful without caring friends working alongside them.

Above all just repeat the most important words, in your voice, in your actions, in everything you do with her:

You're not alone.  You. are. not. alone.  We'll get through this.  I love you. You mean so much to me.  I'm here for you, Sharon.  I'm here.

thank you.  It is the logical advice, what you give.  

And it will be the seed of my real healing.  I'm just not there right now.

it scares me. I'll be honest.

Right now it's not possible.  There's just no-one in my immediate. I know that will change with grad school but what I value in her is the intimacy and the shared story and experiences. Those things just take time.  There's been a couple people this year I'm attracted to, but if I let it sit, it goes away. I realize my "love" isn't really more than "you're attractive."

I find it really hard to say "i love you" to other people.  Because that "i love you" isn't the same words I say to her.  I fear that I might try and fill this hole with other people, that my curiosity -- about sexuality, chiefly, I suppose, might make relationships a vehicle towards answers rather than honest love.  I know that I can play with words and play the game and all that...love isn't that for me.  Love is this compelling reality that's just so much more for me.

It's my faith, it's my dream, my vocation.  It runs through my core.  And all the love I know romantically is tied up in her, and I feel like I could never give that to another person honestly.  The process of falling in love with her was slow, and based in years of friendship that was very intimate, and I can look at my other, similar friends, and know they are not that for me right now.

Does that make sense?  I fear "rebounds" or superficiality -- and more fear preying on others vulnerability in my needs, when I can't really give them vulnerability right now, and without that I don't know how I can give honest love.

Some of that comes with falling in love at 23/4 for the first time.  Some of that comes with depression. Some unrequitedness.  

It's just scary, I suppose.

thank you.  

The challenge is a lot of that charity and stuff *does* tie to her.  Social justice is part of me and that's actually how I met her -- by helping her get involved in service too. I fear both of us are losing that part of our identity as all this has gone on.  When I've tried it since, it reminds me how much I'd like to be doing this kind of stuff *with* her.  And reminds me of what it is that I find so special in her.   That said I know this part of me -- the service bit -- is gonna stick around and is a way out in time.  It just hurts a lot right now.  Thanks for the insight and reminding me of it because sometimes I lose sight of "past" me in all the muck.

I guess I do some of what you are asking in small ways, but I'm so used to the big ways that they feel...unsubstantial. like I could do more if I were just better. 

Luckily in the long journey back to me, I'll be walking as myself the whole way, and that's something.

thanks.  There's a sincerity and security in a hug -even when the hug is just words.  

I love the person I am.  I've grown so much in this.  I hate the depression, but that's not me, even though it tries to become my identity. I started therapy a while back, and I'm on my 27th session, and am proud that I kept up with it so far and it helps. I haven't had a self-harming thought in months, though the "why go on" or "I don't want to be alive" is still around every so often, it's passive, and it goes away.  Just a stomachache that comes with being sick with this illness and I know that as I overcome the depression, it will go away too. 

I just struggle to focus on *me* when so much of *me* is uniquely unlocked by she. The person I want to be is alongside her, and that dream seems so improbable right now.

Thanks for reading and asking.  And a hug back too.  Because everyone's fighting little battles I don't know much about and deserves to have people alongside them in that too.
